# Small/medium compound-border row allocation

Original XML/OPC controls generated by `tools/compound_row_medium_small_fixture.py`,
using the repository's original minimal package skeleton. No corpus content,
third-party artwork, font files or external document engine is included.

The reference application exported `native.pdf` read-only using
`tools/export-reference.ps1`. `tools/record_compound_row_medium_small_pdf.py`
records all 216 row baselines independently and binds source/PDF SHA-256 hashes.
The 24 pages cover both thin/thick orders, small/medium gaps, and sizes
0, 2, 11, 24, 36 and 96 eighth-points. Nine repeated minimum-height rows per
page, exact 12pt Arial lines and zero cell margins isolate accumulated border
allocation from font leading. These new controls do not establish exact-height
row behavior or every possible border size.

Native results distinguish reserved space from painted ink. Small-gap borders
reserve `30 + floor(size * 2.5)` twips; medium-gap borders reserve
`2 * floor(size * 2.5)` twips. Size 11 rules out separately truncating both
half-width bands. Size zero reserves 30/0 twips respectively despite nonzero
painted ink. The painter's existing 600-DPI band widths remain unchanged.

Baseline maximum error was 2.0900pt; corrected maximum is 0.1300pt. Browser
checks every native baseline within the existing .2pt tolerance, plus page
count, no-edit package equality, insertion, unrelated parts, exact undo and
editable reopening. All 24 native/app page pairs were visually reviewed.
These are layout checks, not a claim of pixel-identical PDF/browser rasterization.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38, 17.4.66, 17.4.80 and 17.18.2 describe the border and
row declarations. The numerical twip allocation rule is measured reference behavior;
those clauses do not explicitly prescribe this two-stage rounding pipeline.
